html:
The Guarasugwe, also called Pauserna, were a small Tupi-Guarani people of northeast Bolivia, near the Guaporé River on the border with Brazil. Their language, related to that of the Guarayo, is now extinct.

They lived by farming, hunting and fishing along the rivers. Their neighbours included the Chiquitano and the Itonama. Slave raids, the rubber boom and disease brought their numbers very low, and the last speakers of their language died in the late 1900s in Bolivia.
